content: Hi, I am relatively new to Lean and am just learning the basics of how to use it. There is quite an ambitious formalization project I would like to do which involves formalized mathematical logic, in particular the syntax and model theory of first-order languages. I was wondering if anyone can give me any tips on getting up to speed with how to handle these things in Lean. I have been looking over the formalizedformallogic code repository and I have also been looking at the Flypitch project but it is a bit overwhelming. I would really value any advice about the fastest way of getting on top of it.

Just to narrow down the question, are you looking for information about model theory in lean specifically or lean more in general? I.e. have you already gone through something like #mil and now want to learn the mathlib-isms for fol? I ask because I don't think there is any detailed fol specific introduction to lean, so you will have an easier time if you learn about things like instances and so on in a general math undergraduate context (what MIL does), rather than trying to learn it from the specifics for model theory in mathlib.
Glimpse of Lean contains some very basic exercises about syntax for propositional logic if I remember correctly, that might be less scary than the docs and still wet your appetite.

Yes thanks, I did start working through "Mathematics In Lean" and I thought maybe after a few chapters I could skip through to learning more about how first-order logic is handled, but maybe it would be wiser to just go all the way through that book first?
